cues.text: Some things can be ruined by dry cleaning. Learn to spot them at the counter, before you take them in.
Fake leather, vinyl, and coated fabrics, sometimes called pleather. Solvent can make them peel, crack, or go stiff.
Clothes with glued-on sequins, beads, or gems. The glue can melt and the pieces fall off.
Shirts with rubber, plastic, foil, or glitter prints. The print can crack, melt, or come off.
Bath mats and rugs with a rubber back. The rubber breaks down and crumbles.
Some rain jackets have a waterproof coating that can come off.
A circle with an X on the label means do not dry clean. Follow it.
Real leather and suede need a special leather cleaner. Ask a manager.
Fur and shearling also need a special cleaner. Ask a manager.
If you see one of these, show the customer the part you are worried about.
Write it on the ticket, and ask a manager. Never guess.
